thread:
Alex: quick follow-up on the autoscale stuff. we need a single compactness metric for dedicated GPU pools. goal: balance prewarm latency, idle cost, and eviction churn. thinking of a weighted sum: compactness = a*tail_latency + b*idle_ratio + c*eviction_rate. thoughts?

Jamie: sounds reasonable. couple q's: 1) how do we compute tail_latency (per-tenant p95 cold-start vs cluster-wide?) 2) units normalization for the sum.

Alex: good point. lean per-tenant p95 cold_start to keep fairness. cluster fallback if tenant signal is sparse. we'll normalize each term to [0,1] using historical percentiles.

Sara: expose breakdown please. one scalar is fine for the autoscaler, but product/sales/customers need to see cost vs latency components.

Phil: policy question: who owns weights (a,b,c)? runtime team ships defaults. product can request tenant overrides for SLAs. need RBAC for that.

Mika: +1 to named profiles instead of raw weights: "latency-first", "balanced", "cost-first". map profiles to weight presets. avoids magic numbers in UI.

Jamie: telemetry needs: per-tenant timeseries for cold_start_p95, idle_seconds or idle_ratio, eviction_count (split planned vs unexpected), and a cost_estimate timeseries. labels: tenant, pool, allocation_class (whole/mig), model_size_bucket. granularity 1m.

Alex: jotting a quick table: 
```
metric,labels,granularity
cold_start_p95,tenant,1m
idle_ratio,tenant+pool,1m
unexpected_eviction_count,tenant,1m
planned_eviction_count,tenant,1m
cost_estimate,tenant,1m
```

Phil: treat planned vs unexpected separately in the metric and UI. planned evictions (maintenance, preemption windows) shouldn't penalize compactness.

Sara: billing note: cost_estimate must map to our reserved vs burst accounting. don't confuse the metric with invoice lines. product docs should explain mapping.

Mika: implementation: autoscaler events already include scale_decision. let's add compactness_score + components and the profile used to the event payload.

Jamie: rollout idea: non-binding mode first — compute and emit score but do not act. run for 2 weeks, compare with historical decisions, run offline sims to tune weights.

Alex: yes. non-binding + offline sim, then canary apply to a tiny tenant cohort. also need smoothing/hysteresis to avoid oscillation. propose EMA over 5m and require delta > 0.15 sustained for 3 windows before action.

Phil: edge-case: tenants with short spiky traffic. we must not force long warmups. propose a short-burst escape hatch: allow X seconds of burst without prewarm if under a token/sec budget and charge burst credits.

Mika: admission controller flag "allow_short_burst" consumed via burst credits. won't trigger prewarm but will use burst budget. fine to gate via tenant profile.

Jamie: simulations should include synthetic spike traces and real tenant traces. I can build an offline harness that replays historical load and compares outcomes under current autoscaler vs compactness-driven policy.

Sara: product docs + sales FAQ needed. include examples: "latency-first" => higher cost, lower cold p95; "cost-first" => lower cost, higher p95. also explain billing mapping and burst credits.

Phil: API plan: add /internal/v1/tenant/{id}/autoscale-profile (GET/PUT/PATCH). minimal change. runtime service account + sales/account RBAC can PATCH. log all changes to audit stream.

Alex: auth: only account ops + runtime SA can modify. add audit trail entries with who/when/reason.

Jamie: also add a debug endpoint to fetch recent compactness components for a tenant for troubleshooting.

Mika: telemetry work: I'll extend the proto and add compactness fields to scale_decision events. will emit scores to metrics pipeline and datadog dashboards.

Alex: smoothing: use EMA alpha ~= 0.4 for 1m windows to get ~5m responsive smoothing. hysteresis threshold and cooldown of 3 minutes after an action.

Phil: what about tuning weights per cloud region or pool type? e.g., on-prem customers may prefer cost-first; hosted customers default to latency-first. profiles can be region-aware but defaults set by product tier.

Sara: doc that. sales can request per-customer overrides but we should gate heavy overrides behind contracts.

Jamie: metrics to validate: % of requests hitting cold-start, avg prewarm latency, GPU idle-hours, eviction incidents, and cost delta vs baseline. run A/B for canary.

Alex: next steps owners: Mika -> telemetry + event shape. Jamie -> offline sim harness + smoothing implementation. Phil -> API + RBAC + audit spec. Sara -> product docs + billing mapping. I'll coordinate rollout + runbook.

Mika: will push non-binding scorer to staging and emit a run id.

orch-bot: deploy-notice: non-binding compactness scorer deployed to staging by Mika at 3661234595, run-id: compactness-staging-01

Alex: thanks all. monitor staging dashboards. reconvene in 2 weeks to review sim results and agree canary list. :+1:
